image_description: A live outdoor concert performance featuring a band on an elevated stage. The central figure is a male musician with long blonde hair playing a violin, wearing a black t-shirt and shorts. To his left is another musician in a hat playing guitar/bass, and to the right, a keyboardist or drummer is partially visible. The background consists of large black speaker stacks and trussing structures typical of a festival stage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elevated rectangular platform, raised slightly above floor level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The musicians are clearly standing on a raised surface relative to the implied audience level, confirmed by the presence of stage monitors at their feet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dimensions vary from small intimate platforms to large theatrical stages spanning the full width of a performance hall.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a medium shot focusing on the performers; the full width and total dimensions of the stage are outside the frame and cannot be verified.
The front boundary of the performance area is defined by the line of stage monitors and equipment cases placed along the edge where the musicians are standing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is covered with matte black flooring or painted wood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible floor area around the musicians' feet appears to be a dark, non-reflective surface consistent with standard stage decking or carpet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Steps or ramps provide access from floor level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Access points (stairs/ramps) are typically located at the sides or rear of a stage and are not visible in this frontal/center-focused view.
The top of the frame cuts off before reaching the overhead trussing or lighting rig level; only vertical speaker stacks are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood or metal decking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the specific material grain is obscured by the dark color and shadows, the structural context of a professional concert stage implies standard wood/metal composite decking.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows scuff marks from performances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and lighting conditions do not allow for the detection of fine surface details like scuff marks on the dark flooring.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Side and rear may have wings or backdrop supports.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Large vertical black structures (speaker stacks/wings) are visible on the left and right sides of the frame, serving as lateral boundaries/backdrop supports.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom left corner, white text on black equipment case
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text 'AMA STAGE' (or similar) exhibits slight character deformation and irregular kerning typical of AI-generated text, though it remains largely legible.

artifact_observations.location: Central musician's hands and violin bow
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness and lack of distinct finger definition on the hand holding the violin neck; the bow hair blends slightly into the strings without clear separation.

artifact_observations.location: Microphone stand base and cables near central musician
artifact_observations.reasoning: Cables appear to merge into the stage floor or equipment cases without clear physical grounding or connection points.

selected_experts.reason: To verify the scene classification as a professional concert stage versus a generic platform or street performance.
To accurately locate and identify violins, guitars, microphones, and stage monitors to establish object permanence and count.
To check for fusion artifacts where hands meet instrument necks and bows meet strings, a common failure mode in AI music images.
To rigorously assess the legibility and orthographic correctness of the text on the stage monitors and cases.
To evaluate global lighting consistency and detect any subtle warping in the background trussing or speaker grids.

focus_areas: Structural logic of microphone stands and cables
Consistency of stage elevation and perspective
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the violinist's left hand fingering position; AI often generates impossible chord shapes or fused fingers. Verify if the text on the bottom-left monitor is real English or gibberish. Check if the microphone stands have plausible bases or if they float/merge into the floor.
